subject: Ordinal Manifest Variables and Missing Data

messages.author: ee0aba41dd5807ef
messages.subject: Ordinal Manifest Variables and Missing Data
parts:
Hi Group,

What is the default procedure for missing data when the indicators of a SEM are specified as ordinal? There isn't anything analogous to FIML when DWLS is used as the estimator? 
 
Thanks for your time.
Ross

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Ordinal Manifest Variables and Missing Data
parts: What is the default procedure for missing data when the indicators of a SEM are specified as ordinal? There isn't anything analogous to FIML when DWLS is used as the estimator?

If you peek into the fitted object, you can check and see the "missing" option when you don't explicitly specify it. 

fit@Options$missing

It says "listwise", but I'm not certain whether "listwise" means the same thing in the context of categorical data.  I believe the default in Mplus is pairwise deletion to create contingency tables using all available data, but I don't see "pairwise" as an option on the ?lavaan help page.  Considering WLS can be used even when there are mixed continuous/categorical data, contingency tables for all variables wouldn't always be possible, so I'm curious whether lavaan uses pairwise deletion only for the estimation of thresholds, etc., for ordered categorical variables.

But no, there is not yet a "FIML" analog for non-normal data, unfortunately.

Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Ordinal Manifest Variables and Missing Data
parts:
On 12/08/2013 01:53 AM, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
>
> What is the default procedure for missing data when the indicators
> of a SEM are specified as ordinal? There isn't anything analogous to
> FIML when DWLS is used as the estimator?

Currently (0.5-15), the default is listwise deletion (just like in the
continuous case). Recently, I added the option missing="pairwise", which
you can use when the estimator is not ML.

Yves.
